cls: Antiplatelet agent (P2Y12 ADP receptor inhibitor, cyclopentyltriazolopyrimidine)
pharm: Orally active, directly-acting agent whose parent drug and active metabolite reversibly bind the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor, blocking ADP-mediated signal transduction and platelet activation
tags: ACS / post-MI / CAD / acute ischemic stroke or TIA
BOXED WARNING: use aspirin 75-100 mg/day - higher maintenance aspirin doses reduce ticagrelor effectiveness
quick: 180 mg oral loading dose, then 90 mg twice daily for the first year, then 60 mg twice daily (60 mg twice daily for CAD); use with aspirin 75-100 mg/day
With or without food; may be crushed and mixed with water if needed
Limited human data show no clear drug-associated risk; animal studies showed fetal harm
No dose adjustment, including end-stage renal disease (not dialyzable)
No adjustment in mild; caution in moderate; avoid in severe impairment
No specific interaction; excess raises bleeding/GI risk
Signs of bleeding; dyspnea; digoxin levels with any change in therapy
summary: Ticagrelor is an oral, reversibly-binding P2Y12 platelet inhibitor used with low-dose aspirin to reduce cardiovascular death, MI, and stroke in patients with acute coronary syndrome or a history of MI, to reduce a first MI or stroke in high-risk coronary artery disease, and to reduce stroke after acute ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA. It carries a BOXED WARNING for significant, sometimes fatal bleeding (do not use with active pathological bleeding or a history of intracranial hemorrhage, and do not start before urgent CABG), and a BOXED WARNING that maintenance aspirin doses above 100 mg/day reduce its effectiveness - so it must be paired with aspirin 75-100 mg/day.
indications: Acute coronary syndrome or history of myocardial infarction - to reduce risk of CV death, MI, and stroke; superior to clopidogrel for at least the first 12 months after ACS, and reduces stent thrombosis in patients stented for ACS
Coronary artery disease at high risk with no prior stroke or MI - to reduce risk of a first MI or stroke (efficacy established in a type 2 diabetes mellitus population)
Acute ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale score <=5) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA) - to reduce risk of stroke

dosage.d: 180 mg oral loading dose, then 90 mg twice daily during the first year, then 60 mg twice daily after one year
dosage.n: Give first 90 mg maintenance dose 6-12 h after the load; use with aspirin 75-100 mg daily; after PCI, single antiplatelet therapy with ticagrelor may be considered based on thrombotic vs bleeding risk

dosage.r: Coronary artery disease, no prior stroke or MI
dosage.n: Generally use with aspirin 75-100 mg daily

dosage.r: Acute ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA
dosage.d: 180 mg loading dose, then 90 mg twice daily for up to 30 days
dosage.n: Give first maintenance dose 6-12 h after load; use with aspirin loading dose 300-325 mg then 75-100 mg daily; not recommended if NIHSS >5 or receiving thrombolysis

admin: Give a single 180 mg loading dose, then the maintenance dose twice daily
Always pair with a daily aspirin maintenance dose of 75-100 mg; avoid aspirin doses above what is recommended
May be taken with or without food
If unable to swallow whole, tablets may be crushed, mixed with water, and drunk, or given via nasogastric tube (CH8 or greater)
Do not co-administer with another oral P2Y12 platelet inhibitor
Do not start in patients undergoing urgent CABG
When possible, interrupt therapy 5 days before surgery with major bleeding risk; resume once hemostasis is achieved
Do not stop prematurely - increases risk of MI, stroke, and death
moa: Ticagrelor and its major active metabolite (AR-C124910XX) reversibly interact with the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor to prevent ADP-mediated signal transduction and platelet activation; the two species are approximately equipotent. Unlike thienopyridines, ticagrelor is directly acting (not a prodrug requiring metabolic activation) and binds reversibly, so platelet inhibition tracks with plasma drug levels.

absolute: History of intracranial hemorrhage (high risk of recurrence)
Active pathological bleeding (e.g. peptic ulcer or intracranial hemorrhage)
Hypersensitivity (e.g. angioedema) to ticagrelor or any component
relative: Severe hepatic impairment (avoid use; moderate impairment - weigh risks/benefits)
Acute ischemic stroke/TIA with NIHSS >5 or receiving thrombolysis (not recommended)
Sick sinus syndrome, 2nd/3rd degree AV block, or bradycardia-related syncope without a pacemaker (bradyarrhythmia risk)
Likely need for urgent CABG or other major surgery
Concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers
monitor: Digoxin levels with initiation of or any change in ticagrelor

preg: Available data from case reports of ticagrelor use in pregnant women have not identified a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. In animals, ticagrelor caused structural abnormalities in rat and rabbit offspring at maternal doses about 5 to 7 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) on a body-surface-area basis, and pup death and growth effects in rats dosed during late gestation and lactation at about 10 times the MRHD. Because of the bleeding risk (see BOXED WARNING), weigh benefits and risks when prescribing to a pregnant woman.
lact: There are no data on the presence of ticagrelor or its metabolites in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production. Ticagrelor and its metabolites were present in rat milk at higher concentrations than in maternal plasma, and a drug present in animal milk is likely present in human milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with ticagrelor.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed in renal impairment. In end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, ticagrelor AUC and Cmax were about 38% and 51% higher than in normal renal function, but platelet inhibition was independent of dialysis and similar to healthy adults; ticagrelor is not dialyzable. Efficacy and safety studies did not enroll ESRD patients on dialysis.
hepatic: Ticagrelor is metabolized by the liver, and impaired hepatic function can increase bleeding and other risks. No dosage adjustment is needed in mild hepatic impairment. There is limited experience in moderate impairment - weigh risks and benefits, noting probable increased exposure. Avoid use in severe hepatic impairment, which is likely to increase serum ticagrelor concentrations.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, saquinavir, nelfinavir, indinavir, atazanavir, telithromycin) - substantially increase exposure; avoid
Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g. rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital) - substantially reduce efficacy; avoid
Aspirin >100 mg/day maintenance - reduces ticagrelor effectiveness (BOXED WARNING); use 75-100 mg/day
moderate: Simvastatin or lovastatin - avoid doses above 40 mg (ticagrelor raises their levels)
Rosuvastatin - avoid doses above 20 mg; consider <20 mg if at risk for rhabdomyolysis
Digoxin - ticagrelor inhibits P-glycoprotein; monitor digoxin levels with any change in ticagrelor
Opioids (e.g. morphine, fentanyl) - delay and reduce ticagrelor absorption; consider a parenteral antiplatelet agent in ACS
minor: Moderate CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. diltiazem) - lesser increase in exposure
P-gp inhibitors (e.g. cyclosporine) - increase ticagrelor exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal does not change ticagrelor Cmax but raises AUC by about 21%
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; excess alcohol increases bleeding/GI risk
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause false-negative platelet functional tests (including HIPA assay) for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia; not expected to affect PF4 antibody testing for HIT

common: Bleeding (most common; epistaxis, GI bleeding, bruising, hematuria)
Dyspnea (about 14-21% in trials; usually mild-moderate and self-limiting)
serious: Bradyarrhythmias including AV block and ventricular pauses
rare: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (can occur within <2 weeks of starting)
emergency: Intracranial hemorrhage or other major bleeding
TTP (thrombocytopenia, hemolytic anemia, neurologic signs, renal dysfunction, fever)

monitoring: New, prolonged, or worsened dyspnea (determine if drug-related)
Digoxin levels with initiation of or any change in ticagrelor therapy
ECG / heart rhythm in patients at risk for bradyarrhythmias
Adherence - premature discontinuation raises MI, stroke, and death risk
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed with daily aspirin; do NOT take more than 100 mg of aspirin per day and avoid other aspirin-containing products - higher aspirin doses make ticagrelor less effective
Do not stop taking ticagrelor without talking to your cardiologist - stopping raises the risk of heart attack and stroke
You will bleed and bruise more easily and take longer to stop bleeding; report any unexpected, prolonged, or excessive bleeding, or blood in stool or urine
Contact your doctor if you have unexpected shortness of breath, especially if severe
Tell all doctors and dentists you take ticagrelor before any surgery or dental procedure
If you miss a dose, take your next dose at its scheduled time; do not double up
Breastfeeding is not recommended while taking ticagrelor
pk: Maximum inhibition of platelet aggregation reached around 2 hours after the 180 mg loading dose
Ticagrelor median Tmax about 1.5 h (range 1-4); active metabolite Tmax about 2.5 h; bioavailability ~36%
Approximately 7 hours for ticagrelor and 9 hours for the active metabolite
Maximum platelet inhibition maintained at least 8 hours; reversible - aggregation returns toward baseline by about 5 days after stopping
pearls: BOXED WARNING: can cause significant, sometimes fatal bleeding - do not use in active pathological bleeding or a history of intracranial hemorrhage, and do not start before urgent CABG; if possible manage bleeding without stopping the drug
BOXED WARNING: maintenance aspirin doses above 100 mg/day reduce ticagrelor's effectiveness - always pair with aspirin 75-100 mg/day
Reversible P2Y12 binding (unlike clopidogrel/prasugrel) - faster offset; platelet function recovers over about 5 days, and a missed dose still leaves inhibition similar to clopidogrel trough
Twice-daily dosing; dose steps down from 90 mg to 60 mg BID after the first year post-ACS
Dyspnea is common (~14-21%), usually mild and self-limiting; no specific treatment needed if drug-related
Can cause ventricular pauses/bradyarrhythmias; avoid in unprotected sick sinus syndrome or high-grade AV block
Not dialyzable and platelet transfusion does not reverse its effect - manage bleeding supportively
Avoid strong CYP3A inhibitors and inducers; monitor digoxin and limit simvastatin/lovastatin to <=40 mg and rosuvastatin to <=20 mg
missed: If you miss a dose, do not take an extra dose to make up for it. Simply take your next dose at its regularly scheduled time. Because ticagrelor binds reversibly, a single missed dose still leaves platelet inhibition similar to the trough seen with clopidogrel.
overdose: There is no known treatment to reverse ticagrelor, and it is not dialyzable. Bleeding is the expected effect of overdose - provide supportive measures; platelet transfusion did not reverse the antiplatelet effect in healthy volunteers and is unlikely to help. Other effects may include gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) or ventricular pauses - monitor the ECG and follow local standard medical practice.
